finding.title: Use DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() instead of raw DateTime.now() for insert timestamps in epic_18/epic_19 story-acceptance tests
finding.why: TQ-6 requires tests use a fixed DateTimeFactory rather than the wall clock. None of these 15 sites are currently asserted on, so there is no live flake today — but the codebase already has a working seam (DateTimeFactory.nowUtc(), used correctly by test/helpers/drift_memory.dart's seedProfile in the very same suite and throughout production DAOs) that these two files bypass with raw DateTime.now(). The next author who copies one of these insert blocks into a test that does compare timestamps (an ordering check, a 'recently updated' window) inherits non-determinism silently.
finding.recommendation: Replace DateTime.now() with DateTimeFactory.nowUtc() (or a fixed literal) at all 15 sites, matching the pattern already used in test/helpers/drift_memory.dart.

finding.title: Split oversized story-acceptance files over AG-3's 400-line cap: epic_21_multi_account_test.dart (1048 lines), epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart (423 lines)

evidence.quote: /// Story acceptance tests for Epic 21 -- Multi-Account Device.
/// Story acceptance tests for Epic 24 — Stop-the-Bleeding (Phase 0).

finding.why: Both files exceed the 400-line agent-context-budget ratchet by 1.06x-2.6x (1048 and 423 lines respectively, verified via wc -l). Content past an agent's read window is effectively invisible, so new stories tend to get appended blind or forked into a fresh file instead of merged into the right group -- which is exactly what already happened for Epic 24 (see the duplicate-file finding below).
finding.recommendation: Split epic_21_multi_account_test.dart by story group (e.g. epic_21_registry_test.dart / epic_21_lifecycle_test.dart) and epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart by story (24.1 rules vs 24.4 crashlytics), matching the epic_25_story_NN_* convention already used for later epics; update Makefile targets to match.
acceptance_criteria: `find lib test -name '*.dart' ! -name '*.g.dart' ! -name '*.freezed.dart' | xargs wc -l | awk '$1>400'` reports zero lines for these two files
All existing test groups/tags still run under their current `make test-epic-*`/`--tags` invocations after the split

finding.title: Merge or clearly disambiguate epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart and epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart; make test-epic-24 run both

evidence.quote: /// Story acceptance tests for Epic 24 -- Stop-the-Bleeding (Phase 0).
/// Story acceptance tests for Epic 24 — Stop-the-Bleeding (Phase 0).
test-epic-24: ## Run all Epic 24 (Stop-the-Bleeding) acceptance tests

finding.why: make test-epic-24's own doc-comment claims to run 'all Epic 24' tests but only executes epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart (Stories 24.7/24.8); Stories 24.1 and 24.4's 423 lines of tests, living in the near-identically-named epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart, are silently excluded, and there is no test-story-24.1/test-story-24.4 target at all. A developer following CLAUDE.md's documented loop ('Run make test-epic-N to check you didn't break sibling stories') gets a false all-clear for 24.1/24.4 while iterating on 24.7/24.8. Git history confirms this isn't an in-progress rename: both files were independently created the same day (2026-05-13) by different work streams (DNI-310 vs DNI-316/319), each assuming it owned 'the' epic-24 file -- the exact 'divergent parallel copy' failure mode AG-4/AG-5's rationale warns about. (The tests still execute under `make ci` -> `flutter test --coverage`'s whole-directory discovery, so the CI hard gate itself isn't bypassed -- only the convenience per-epic/per-story targets are broken.)
finding.recommendation: Rename/merge into one canonical, clearly-named file (or split by story with unambiguous suffixes the way epic_25+ do, e.g. epic_24_story_24_1_rules_test.dart), then add test-story-24.1/test-story-24.4 Makefile targets and fix test-epic-24 to cover all four stories.
acceptance_criteria: `make test-epic-24` output shows Stories 24.1, 24.4, 24.7, and 24.8 all executing
Only one file (or a story-suffixed set) matches `test/story_acceptance/epic_24_*_test.dart` with no name differing from another only by an article/qualifier word

finding.title: Replace tautological verifyNever(mockFacade...) checks on a facade never injected into the repo under test in epic_24_stop_bleeding_test.dart
finding.why: Both 'no push when syncEngine is null (local-born user)' tests construct localRepo without a syncEngine: argument (defaults to null), so localRepo never holds a reference to mockFacade. Mocktail records invocations per mock instance, so verifyNever(() => mockFacade....) is checking an object the code under test never touches -- it passes unconditionally no matter what localRepo actually does internally. A regression that made a local-born repository push to Firestore through any other path would not be caught by this acceptance test despite its name promising exactly that guarantee, and the production code's current correct `_syncEngine?.push...` null-guard (verified in both TrackRepositoryImpl and LearningOrderRepositoryImpl) is protected by nothing but the fact the call would crash first.
finding.recommendation: Delete the vacuous verifyNever calls (the preceding await already fails the test if a null syncEngine crashes on use), or replace with an assertion tied to localRepo's actual collaborators -- e.g. assert the local Drift write succeeded with no corresponding outbox/sync artifact.
acceptance_criteria: Neither 'no push when syncEngine is null' test references a mock object that isn't reachable from the object under test
A deliberately-introduced bug that makes the null-syncEngine path push anyway (e.g. via a stray ambient reference) fails one of these two tests

finding.title: Scope firestore.rules text-matching assertions to their collection block and check deny-all ordering in epic_24_stop_the_bleeding_test.dart
finding.rule: TQ-8 (weak assertion vs SR-1..3 rule content)

evidence.quote: // The deny-all rule must come before any collection-specific rules.
final denyPos = rules.indexOf('allow read, write: if false');

finding.why: 'allows create' and 'enforces completed_at' assert against the whole `rules` string instead of the `_extractBlock(rules, 'completions/{completionId}')` result that the very next test in the same group ('denies update on completions') correctly uses. Nothing stops the points-bound or timestamp-clamp text from being removed from the completions block and coincidentally still matching elsewhere in the file (e.g. another append-only ledger) while this test stays green -- points_ledger and streak_events currently have no such bound at all, so a future accidental swap would go undetected. Separately, the deny-all test's own comment states the rule 'must come before any collection-specific rules' but the assertion only checks `denyPos > -1` (string exists somewhere) -- it never compares denyPos to any collection match's position, so reordering the deny-all rule after a permissive collection rule would not fail this test despite the comment's explicit claim.
finding.recommendation: Change the two unscoped assertions to use `_extractBlock(rules, 'completions/{completionId}')` like the sibling test three lines below; change the deny-all test to assert `denyPos < rules.indexOf('match /completions')` (or the first collection match position) instead of just `> -1`.
acceptance_criteria: The two completions assertions call _extractBlock(rules, 'completions/{completionId}') the same way the 'denies update' test does
The deny-all test fails if the deny-all rule is moved after a collection-specific match block
